      packages:

# FIRST HALF – The claim and its reproduction {#first-half-the-claim-and-its-reproduction .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
First half
:::

::: notes
The first half takes us from three kinds of repetition and the robustness study, as I knew it from the inside, to the paper and its record in SCORE. You write the question that the claim answers, in one sentence, in your notes, and before the break you reproduce the result recorded by one of three analysts, to the third decimal, and find out why the three analysts arrived at different numbers.
:::

# SECOND HALF – The multiverse of the claim {#second-half-the-multiverse-of-the-claim .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Second half
:::

::: notes
Welcome back. In the first half you reproduced a recorded number, and in this half you become the sixth analyst and make choices of your own. I open the menu of the fourteen decisions that any analysis of this claim has to take, starting with the survey decisions, and show the code that sits behind it. You then work the menu on the slides and send the analysis that you would defend to the class chart, which we read against the curve of every justifiable analysis of these data, before we turn to what such a curve can and cannot establish. We end on the critics of the multiverse, on what a preregistration would add, and on the replication of this claim with new data.
:::
